# Incident Report: Fake-Invoice JS Downloader → C2 Loader Infection

**Evidence:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (only artifact present in the evidence folder; no separate IDS/Suricata export was included, so all indicators below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark).

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (confirmed via ARP and consistent Ethernet source on all outbound traffic) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| Windows domain | lafontainebleu.org (AD domain; DC is WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (seen as Kerberos CNameString `plucero` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 10.8.15.133) |

## Malware family and attribution

**Behaviorally consistent with Latrodectus** (an IcedID-derived downloader/loader family distributed via fake shipping-invoice phishing pages). This is a **behavioral, not signature-confirmed**, attribution — no IDS/Suricata alert export was provided in the evidence set, so nothing here is backed by a rule match.

Basis for the behavioral call, all observed directly in the pcap:
- Delivery via a fake FedEx tracking/invoice lure domain, dropping a ZIP containing a single oversized `.js` downloader.
- The `.js` file (6,990,020 bytes) is padded with megabytes of garbage text lifted from unrelated academic/report documents, wrapped in `/* ... */` comment blocks around small real script fragments (`WScript.Sleep(10000)` was found embedded mid-padding) — a known evasion/AV-bloat technique used by this loader family.
- The script contains a hardcoded callback URL to the same phishing domain (`business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...`) used purely for tracking/beaconing, not content.
- After execution, the host fetched a PE32+ x86-64 DLL from a hardcoded raw IP (no DNS lookup precedes the connection) over plain HTTP.
- The infected host then generated 308 HTTP requests to that same IP over ~30 minutes, almost all `GET`/`POST /` with encrypted/binary bodies, most answered `400 Bad Request` — consistent with a C2 beacon that fell out of sync with its server, a pattern documented for Latrodectus C2 traffic.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed in traffic)

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70 (Cloudflare-fronted)

**Malicious URL (initial ZIP delivery)**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (frame 6418, HTTP 200, 2,767,804 bytes → ZIP archive)

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — raw IP, no DNS resolution observed; 308 HTTP requests over 04:11:58–04:42:26 (UTC+4), plaintext HTTP carrying encrypted/binary payloads, mostly answered with `400 Bad Request`.
- Payload staging URL on the same host: `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (frame 10611/10762, HTTP 200, 159,232 bytes → PE32+ DLL)

**Transferred files and hashes**

| File | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js (inside the ZIP from quote.checkfedexexp.com) | 6,990,020 bytes | dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c |
| managements (the ZIP download itself) | 2,767,804 bytes | 798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5 |
| 0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4 (DLL fetched from C2 IP) | 159,232 bytes | b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6 |

## Timeline (relative order, same session)

1. **10.8.15.133** GET's `/managements?...` from `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70) → downloads ZIP containing `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`.
2. JS downloader executes on host (Sleep/timer logic embedded in comment padding).
3. Host resolves and TLS-connects to `business.checkfedexexp.com` — tracking/callback beacon.
4. Host HEAD/GET's `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` → downloads 159,232-byte PE32+ DLL.
5. Host begins sustained C2 beaconing to `72.5.43.29:80` (308 requests, ~30 minutes), consistent with the DLL loading and running as the persistent C2 agent.

All other traffic from the host (Bing/MSN/Office/Windows Update/Adobe/Edge telemetry) is legitimate background noise from a Windows 10/11 + Edge 127 workstation and is not part of the infection chain.
